Trust us to handle the tough work, reducing future risks and helping your property bounce back.

text.text: At Givens Fire & Forestry LLC , we are more than just a tree service—we are your dedicated partners in creating safe, resilient, and fire-resistant landscapes. Founded by Samuel Givens, a veteran wildland firefighter, our company has grown from a local Montana operation into a regional leader in wildfire mitigation and environmentally conscious land management.

Serving Montana, with plans to expand soon into the Greater Spokane, Washington area, our team brings decades of combined "on-the-line" firefighting experience to every property we service. We specialize in:
Wildfire mitigation: using frontline tactics to create defensible space
Tree health and hazard removal: identifying risks before they become emergencies
Sustainable forestry: managing land with an eye toward long-term ecological health

Our mission is simple: to empower homeowners with the knowledge and professional services needed to protect their investments while enhancing the natural beauty of Big Sky Country and the Inland Northwest.

Throughout his time on the frontlines, Samuel has served in multiple critical leadership roles, including Incident Commander Type 5 (ICT5), Crew Boss Trainee, and Certified Faller. His intimate understanding of wildfire behavior and forest health was forged in the heat of active fire management, giving him a unique perspective on how to effectively mitigate risk before a fire ever starts.

Samuel’s passion extends beyond the field and into education; he is dedicated to empowering homeowners with "fire-smart" strategies and sustainable land management solutions. By combining technical expertise with a lifelong dedication to forestry, Samuel ensures that every project in the Montana division is executed with precision, care, and a focus on long-term environmental resilience.

As the founder of Givens Fire & Forestry LLC, Samuel Givens has built a career centered on a deep commitment to protecting homes and communities from the devastating effects of wildfires. Based in Montana, Samuel brings over seven years of nationwide wildland firefighting experience to the lead of our Montana operations.

Robert’s firefighting career has taken him across the North American continent, spanning the Western United States and Canada—including Oregon, Washington, California, Utah, Idaho, Montana, Colorado, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan. This extensive "on-the-ground" experience across diverse terrains gives him a specialized understanding of fire behavior and fuel management in various climates.

Now based in the greater Spokane area, Robert is preparing to serve the local community as part of our upcoming expansion into Eastern Washington . His mission is to help Inland Northwest property owners mitigate tree hazards and implement proven defensible space strategies, ensuring homes and families are better protected from the ever-present threat of wildfire.

As a key operator supporting our planned Eastern Washington expansion , Robert Berry brings a decade of unique environmental experience and a deep-seated passion for forest stewardship to Givens Fire & Forestry. Robert’s career began in the rugged landscapes of Southeast Alaska, where he spent 10 years living and working on the edge of the Tongass National Forest. This immersion in one of the world’s most complex ecosystems laid the foundation for his transition into professional wildland firefighting in 2020.

text.text: | DEFENSIBLE SPACE CONSULTING | POST BURN CLEAN-UP | SLASH PILE REMOVAL | HAZARDOUS TREE REMOVAL | WILDFIRE FUEL MITIGATION | BRUSH PILE REMOVAL |

This forest scene demonstrates classic wildfire hazards we commonly address in Montana, where over 940,000 acres burned in 2021 alone. You can see the dangerous conditions: densely packed trees with touching canopies, multiple layers of vegetation creating ladder fuels, and thick understory growth. Note the overcrowded birch trees in the foreground and heavy ground vegetation. The wooden cabin visible in the background is particularly vulnerable under these conditions, which could rapidly carry fire from the ground to the tree crowns - a scenario that contributed to Montana's $347 million in fire suppression costs between 2017-2021.

Following our professional mitigation work by former wildland firefighters, observe the dramatic improvement in defensible space - a critical factor given that homes with proper defensible space are 75% more likely to survive a wildfire. We've strategically removed selected trees to create proper spacing, eliminated ladder fuels, and cleared excess ground vegetation, following Montana DNRC guidelines. The forest floor is now maintained with a natural mulch layer from chipped materials. Notice how the remaining trees are well-spaced while still providing shade and aesthetic value. The path created provides both access for maintenance and a natural fire break. This strategic approach not only protects structures but helps preserve healthy forest ecology - critical in Montana where an average of 1,800 wildfires occur annually
While Montana faces massive acreage threats, the Spokane area carries some of the highest structure-risk in the nation.

In Spokane County alone, over 44,000 homes are considered at high to extreme risk of wildfire damage. We don’t just clear brush; we follow Washington DNR 'Firewise' standards to give your home a fighting chance in the Inland Northwest’s unique 'Home Ignition Zone'

As certified Class C Fallers and former wildland firefighters, we specialize in removing the most challenging hazardous trees that threaten property and safety. In our firefighting careers, we've safely dropped trees up to 45" diameter under extreme conditions - now we bring that expertise to your property.

What makes a tree hazardous? Dead standing snags that could fall any moment. Storm-damaged leaners with split tops. Disease-killed giants threatening structures. Widow-makers with dangerous overhead branches. The harsh conditions of the Inland Northwest and Big Sky Country create all these hazards and more.

Our expertise extends to the specific health threats of the Inland Northwest. Eastern Washington is currently seeing a massive surge in tree mortality from Douglas-fir beetles and Ips pine engravers , which have affected hundreds of thousands of acres recently. If your pines are turning red or dropping needles, they aren't just dying—they are becoming high-intensity fuel for the next fire season. We specialize in identifying and removing these 'standing matches' before they threaten your home

Our advanced falling techniques come from years of fireline experience: precision directional falling, bore cutting for control, multiple wedge sets for accuracy. When the job demands it, we deploy heavy machinery and professional rigging systems. With hazard trees contributing to over 100 firefighter fatalities in two decades, we take safety seriously.

From single dangerous trees to complex technical removals requiring crane support, we handle what others won't touch. Because after managing the most dangerous trees under the worst fire conditions, we know exactly how to protect your property from hazard trees.
What is Slash, and Why Should You Remove It?

Slash refers to tree limbs, branches, and debris left behind from land clearing, tree removal, or forestry work. If left unmanaged, these piles become a major fire hazard, providing fuel for wildfires and increasing the risk to your home and property. Over time, slash piles also attract pests and contribute to poor land health, making proper disposal essential for both safety and environmental reasons.

We provide safe and efficient slash pile removal tailored to your property’s needs. Whether you need hauling, chipping, or on-site disposal, we handle everything to ensure compliance with fire safety regulations. Our team evaluates your land, determines the best removal method, and leaves your property safer and cleaner.

In areas where burning is permitted, we offer controlled slash pile burns and larger-scale field burning services. With expert wildland firefighter supervision and strict safety measures, we ensure that burns are conducted responsibly, reducing fire hazards while maintaining soil health. We handle permits, timing, and execution, so you can rest easy knowing the job is done safely and effectively.

Wildfires leave behind dangerous debris, from burned structures to hazardous ash and unstable trees. Proper cleanup is crucial to ensuring safety and preventing further damage. We specialize in the careful removal of fire-damaged homes, sheds, and other structures while prioritizing the safe handling of hazardous materials. Our team also works to recover any salvageable belongings, offering homeowners peace of mind during the recovery process.

After the fire is out, the land remains at risk. Burned vegetation weakens soil stability, increasing the chances of erosion, mudslides, and sediment runoff. Our team clears hazardous trees and brush, stabilizes the soil, and helps reintroduce native plant life to promote natural recovery. By addressing these risks early, we ensure your property remains both safe and environmentally healthy.
Comprehensive Cleanup for a Fresh Start

Every wildfire recovery is unique, and we tailor our services to meet your specific needs. Whether you need full-site clearing, selective cleanup, or assistance with hazardous debris, we have the expertise and equipment to handle it efficiently. Our goal is not just to remove the remnants of destruction but to help you move forward with a clean, stable, and safer property.

Looking at the first image, we see a dense, overgrown area with thick vegetation. The brush is tangled and chaotic, with fallen debris, dead branches, and thick undergrowth creating a cluttered forest floor. This impenetrable wall of vegetation creates a dangerous fuel ladder that allows fire to spread rapidly across property lines and climb into treetops. The natural drainage channel is barely visible beneath the accumulated brush, wildlife habitat is compromised, and sunlight struggles to penetrate the dense canopy, hindering forest health.

The transformation is remarkable! The second image shows the same area after professional brush clearing. The natural drainage path is now clearly defined with smooth stones visible along the bottom, reducing erosion risks. The surrounding vegetation has been strategically thinned, creating essential defensible space while allowing healthy trees to remain. Sunlight now penetrates to the forest floor, promoting diverse plant growth and improved wildlife habitat. The clear separation between ground vegetation and tree canopies breaks the fuel ladder—a crucial element of fire prevention that reduces potential fire intensity and enhances overall property aesthetics and usability.

From the heavy 'snow-load' of Southwest Montana to the notorious windstorms and ice events of the Spokane Valley, our teams are ready. Storm-damaged trees in Washington often involve 'widow-makers' hung up in dense Ponderosa canopies—technical removals that require the precision of a certified faller.

When severe weather hits, downed trees and debris don't just create safety hazards—they dramatically increase wildfire fuel loads on your property. Our emergency storm removal service delivers rapid response to clear fallen timber, damaged branches, and storm debris before they become bigger problems. We bring specialized equipment and experienced crews who understand the urgency of the situation, safely removing hazardous trees from structures, access roads, and critical infrastructure.

Storm damage requires more than just cleanup—it demands expertise in hazard assessment and strategic removal. Our team evaluates structural damage, identifies unstable trees that pose ongoing threats, and executes controlled removal operations that protect your buildings and landscape. We handle everything from large-diameter trees suspended on structures to widespread debris fields, ensuring your property is restored to a safe condition while simultaneously reducing future wildfire risk. When the unexpected happens, we're ready to respond with the equipment, skills, and speed your emergency demands.

With dedicated crews based in Three Forks, MT , and expanding soon to Spokane, WA , we proudly serve homeowners and landowners across Southwest Montana , with Inland Northwest services launching soon . Whether you need wildfire mitigation, tree removal, or post-burn cleanup, our team is ready to assist. Reach out today to schedule a consultation or join our Spokane-area interest list.

text.text: Educational Resources for Wildfire Mitigation and Forest Management

At Givens Fire & Forestry LLC, we believe in empowering homeowners and landowners with the knowledge they need to protect their properties. Below are some trusted resources that provide valuable information on wildfire prevention, forest management, and general safety measures. Whether you're just starting to learn about fire mitigation or you're looking to expand your knowledge, these links can help you take the necessary steps to safeguard your land.
Montana State University Extension Forestry Calendar

The Montana State University Extension Forestry Calendar is a comprehensive resource for individuals interested in forestry and natural resource management. It provides a detailed schedule of upcoming events, workshops, and educational opportunities throughout Montana, catering to both landowners and professionals.

Participants can engage in a variety of activities designed to enhance their understanding of forest health, fire prevention, and sustainable land management practices. These events cover topics such as forest ecology, fire and insect management for resilience, wildlife habitat enhancement, understory and range management, and forest assessment and maintenance. Additionally, workshops on writing Forest Stewardship Management Plans and resources for further assistance are available.

The National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) Incident Management Situation Report (IMSR) is a crucial daily publication that offers in-depth insights into wildfire incidents across the United States. It provides detailed information on active fires, fire weather conditions, and the various resources being mobilized to manage these incidents. By keeping up with these reports, homeowners, land managers, and emergency responders can stay informed about fire activity trends, anticipate potential threats, and understand the ongoing coordinated efforts to protect communities and critical infrastructure. This valuable resource helps in making informed decisions about fire preparedness and response.

The Fire Weather & Avalanche Center provides real-time, comprehensive wildfire and avalanche forecasts, maps, and analysis to help you stay informed about hazardous conditions in your area. This site offers detailed fire weather reports, including temperature, wind speed, humidity, and precipitation forecasts, which are essential for understanding and assessing wildfire risks. It also provides avalanche forecasts with snowpack conditions, danger ratings, and safety recommendations for mountainous regions. Whether you're a homeowner, landowner, or fire prevention professional, this resource is crucial for staying ahead of environmental factors that impact safety and fire prevention efforts.

Firewise USA is a program developed by the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) to empower communities in reducing wildfire risks. The program offers a wealth of valuable resources, strategies, and practical tips designed to help homeowners and communities take proactive steps to prepare for and protect properties from wildfires. By becoming part of Firewise USA, you gain access to tools, expert advice, and best practices for creating defensible spaces, reducing fire hazards, and improving your property’s resilience to wildfires. It’s an essential initiative for anyone looking to safeguard their home and neighborhood from the devastating impacts of wildfire.

The Anchor Point Podcast is a dedicated resource for the wildland firefighting community, offering deep, insightful discussions on a wide range of topics including fire behavior, safety protocols, and the mental health challenges faced by firefighters. The podcast features candid interviews with industry professionals, shedding light on both the personal and professional aspects of the job. Each episode serves as a platform for sharing valuable knowledge and experiences, encouraging learning, growth, and reflection among those in the field. By highlighting the often-overlooked emotional and psychological impacts of wildland firefighting, the podcast fosters a sense of connection and support within the community. Anchor Point Podcast provides essential insights and resources for navigating the complexities of the profession while promoting mental well-being and safety on the job.

The Hotshot Wake Up is a powerful podcast that offers unfiltered and authentic perspectives from the world of wildland firefighting. Hosted by seasoned firefighters with years of firsthand experience, the show delves into the unique challenges, intense experiences, and invaluable lessons learned in this high-stakes and demanding profession.The podcast emphasizes the importance of community support, resilience, and education, providing a platform for discussing mental and physical well-being, stress management, and the critical need for a supportive environment within the firefighting community. Hotshot Wake Up offers insightful stories and candid conversations that bring attention to the human side of firefighting.

This portal serves as a comprehensive hub for both wildland firefighters and the general public, offering a wide range of resources and training programs. It includes in-depth courses on essential topics such as fire prevention, safety protocols, and best practices for reducing the risk of wildfires. Whether you’re a firefighter looking to advance your skills or a homeowner and community member interested in safeguarding your property, this site provides valuable tools, knowledge, and expert advice to help protect lives and property from the dangers of wildfires. With a focus on real-world strategies, the portal empowers users to take proactive measures to reduce fire hazards, enhance community preparedness, and respond effectively to wildfire threats. It’s a vital resource for anyone looking to contribute to wildfire risk reduction and safety.

The Montana Department of Natural Resources and Conservation offers grants designed to help landowners reduce hazardous fuels and enhance wildfire safety on their properties. These grants can cover a range of services, including brush removal, tree thinning, and creating defensible space. If you're looking to reduce fire risks on your land, you may be eligible for funding to help pay for the services your property needs. Visit this link to find out more and see if you qualify for this valuable assistance, which can help cover the cost of the work provided by our experienced team.

text.text: Here are two useful tools for tree measurements and calculations. Click on the tool names or the images below to start using them!

Got a felled tree and want to know how much firewood you’ve got? This tool calculates the tree’s volume based on diameter and height, then converts it into cords of wood. Ideal for firewood sellers, homesteaders, and loggers who need quick and accurate estimates

Want to estimate a tree’s height without climbing it? This tool helps you calculate tree height using a simple angle measurement method. Just input your distance from the tree and the angle of elevation, and get an instant height calculation.
